verified.exploit_entry_point: The library's public API: the Address4 and Address6 constructors and their special-range predicates (isPrivate, isLoopback, isLinkLocal, isMulticast, isUnspecified, isULA, isDocumentation, is6to4, isMapped4). Every security case constructs one of these classes from a literal and reads one predicate; the functional group also runs the project's own functionality-v4/v6 mocha suites for the affected area.
sites: src/ipv6.ts:567-575 (getType matches the type table through the shared subnet primitive)
src/ipv6.ts:1203-1213 (isLinkLocal compares 64 bits against fe80:0:0:0, not the fe80::/10 table entry at src/v6/constants.ts:47)
src/ipv6.ts:1219-1220, 1267-1268, 1283-1284 (isMulticast/isLoopback/isUnspecified decide on the getType string, which has no ::ffff:0:0/96 entry at src/v6/constants.ts:25-53)
src/ipv6.ts:1243-1245, 1476-1480 (isMapped4 and the subnet constants; no NAT64 well-known constant and no embedded-IPv4 delegation)
src/ipv6.ts:1291-1293 (no private check on Address6 at all, so the NAT64 local-use entry at src/v6/constants.ts:52 has no public/internal answer)
src/common.ts:10-12 (isInSubnet returns false when the address's own prefix is shorter than the checked range)
src/ipv4.ts:456-506 (every IPv4 special-range predicate is built on that primitive)
routes: T1: IPv4-mapped (::ffff:0:0/96) and NAT64 well-known (64:ff9b::/96) values through isLoopback, isLinkLocal, isMulticast, isUnspecified
T2: native link-local addresses anywhere in fe80::/10 outside fe80::/64
T3: host addresses written with a CIDR prefix shorter than the checked range, through Address4/Address6 classifiers
T4: the NAT64 local-use block 64:ff9b:1::/48 through isPrivate
Coupled values kept: isInSubnet network-containment semantics, getScope/getType results for existing range classes, RFC 6052 encode/decode vectors and defaults, and the existing special-range answers
verified.project_tests_run: The project's own functionality-v4-test.ts and functionality-v6-test.ts (258 test cases) run headlessly with mocha + tsx on the pinned tree, the reference fix, and every check patch; 11 hidden functional cases and 23 hidden security cases add the behavioural coverage.

traps.shape: an IPv6 value that carries an IPv4 address (IPv4-mapped ::ffff:0:0/96 and the NAT64 well-known prefix 64:ff9b::/96) is classified by its wrapper: isLoopback/isLinkLocal/isMulticast/isUnspecified proxy through getType, and the type table has no mapped entry, so a mapped loopback, link-local, multicast or unspecified address reads as an ordinary global unicast
traps.reason_to_dismiss: isMapped4() already checks the mapped bits directly and getType() already names the well-known NAT64 prefix, so the wrapper looks handled and the predicates look IPv6-native; the advisory's named 'missing private check' reads as API parity, not as misclassification
traps.realistic_because: published advisory route (GHSA-22jq-vg5j-6vgg) at the pinned commit; the source fix added embeddedIPv4() and delegated these predicates

traps.shape: link-local classification compares the first 64 bits against fe80:0:0:0 while the type table recognises fe80::/10, so an address in the rest of the /10 is reported as link-local by getType and not by isLinkLocal
traps.reason_to_dismiss: the in-code comment says zeroes are required and that isInSubnet with 'fe80::/10' cannot be used, which reads as a deliberate decision, and getType() already calls the same addresses link-local
traps.realistic_because: real, unmodified upstream code: the 64-bit check survives both published fixes and the later host-bits rewrite in the pinned line

traps.shape: every special-range classifier is built on isInSubnet, which returns false whenever the address's own CIDR prefix is shorter than the checked range, so a host written with a short suffix is reported as outside ranges it belongs to
traps.reason_to_dismiss: the short-circuit is the correct meaning of subnet containment (a /8 is not inside a /9), the project's own tests pin it, and a host address with a CIDR suffix is documented and produced by legitimate subnet arithmetic
traps.realistic_because: real, unmodified upstream code: the project split host classification from subnet containment in a later release, after this pin; the natural relax-the-primitive fix is proved wrong by functional_overbroad.patch

traps.shape: the NAT64 local-use block 64:ff9b:1::/48 is named by the type table but has no public/internal answer; the embedded IPv4 cannot be decoded without the deployment's RFC 6052 prefix length, so an embedded-address-only private check leaves the whole block public
traps.reason_to_dismiss: getType() already returns 'NAT64 (local-use)', the decode default is documented as the well-known prefix, and the local-use prefix length is operator-chosen, so returning null (and the absence of a private check) reads as the contract
traps.realistic_because: published advisory route (GHSA-2vr4-cq9g-pvrc): the fix of the fix on top of the mapped/NAT64 normalization

patch_checks.why: fresh agent (deepseek-flash[1m]), full view (instruction, tree, tests, reference, trap list)

wrong_fix_catalogue.refuse_all: n/a: the product is a pure classifier with no deny path; a check that reports every address internal fails the public-address cases and the project's own tests, so the class has no separate refusal analogue
wrong_fix_catalogue.crash_as_refusal: n/a: a throw or crash fails the case outright; no test treats an exception as an acceptable outcome
wrong_fix_catalogue.one_role_or_direction: n/a: no roles, peers or directions exist on this surface; every security case drives the same public classifiers
wrong_fix_catalogue.reads_only: n/a: the operation is pure address classification; there is no read/write or verb split
wrong_fix_catalogue.missing_authority: n/a: nothing looks up an authority, secret or role; the library is self-contained

A.summary: misclassification of IPv4-mapped/NAT64 IPv6 addresses can bypass SSRF and trust-boundary checks

B.summary: no classifier recognizes the NAT64 local-use range 64:ff9b:1::/48
